ing: bryndza, or feta mashed with a spoon of cream cheese
st: Squeeze the grated potatoes in a clean towel to remove extra water.
Mix potatoes, [[1.5 cup]] flour, 1 egg and [[1.5 tsp]] salt into a thick sticky batter.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Press the batter through a large-holed colander or spaetzle press into the water in batches, or scrape small bits from a board with a knife.
Boil each batch for 3 minutes until the dumplings float. Lift out with a slotted spoon.
Fry the bacon in a skillet over medium heat for 8 minutes until crisp.
Mix the warm dumplings with the cheese and [[0.25 cup]] sour cream until creamy.
Top with bacon and its fat, and chives. Serve hot.
Put the pork in a pot with [[8 cup]] water and bay leaves. Simmer 30 minutes.
Add the sauerkraut with its juice, mushrooms and prunes. Simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the sausage and cook 10 minutes more.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] lard in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] flour, the garlic and [[1 tbsp]] paprika for 1 minute. Add a ladle of soup to loosen it.
Stir this mix into the pot and simmer 10 minutes until the soup thickens.
Check the pork is cooked to 145°F (63°C) or more and season with salt.
Serve with a spoon of sour cream.
Squeeze the grated potato in a towel to remove moisture.
Mix with [[1.5 cup]] flour, the egg and [[1 tsp]] salt into a thick dough.
Boil salted water. Push or scrape small bits of dough into the water in batches.
Cook each batch for 3 minutes until the dumplings float. Drain.
Fry the bacon in a large skillet for 7 minutes until crisp. Remove, leaving the fat.
Cook the onion in the fat for 5 minutes. Add the sauerkraut and cook 8 minutes.
Add the dumplings and bacon. Toss on medium heat for 3 minutes.
Season with [[0.5 tsp]] pepper and salt, and serve hot.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes. Drain and mash with the cheese and salt for the filling.
Mix [[3 cup]] flour, 1 egg, [[0.75 cup]] warm water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Knead 8 minutes. Rest 20 minutes.
Roll the dough about 1/8 inch thick and cut 3-inch circles.
Put a spoon of filling on each circle, fold over and pinch the edges tightly.
Boil in salted water for 6 minutes until they float.
Fry the bacon and onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Toss the dumplings in [[4 tbsp]] butter.
Top with bacon, onion and [[0.5 cup]] sour cream.

ing: cut in 4 slices about 0.5 inch thick, or Gouda
st: Freeze the cheese slices for 20 minutes so they hold their shape.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] mayonnaise with the pickles, capers and [[1 tsp]] lemon juice for the tartar sauce.
Dip each cheese slice in flour, then the beaten egg, then breadcrumbs. Repeat the egg and breadcrumbs for a thick coat.
Heat the oil to 340°F (170°C) in a deep pan.
Fry the potato fries in batches for 6 minutes until golden. Drain and salt.
Fry the cheese for 2 minutes per side until deep golden. Do not let it sit too long or it will leak.
Drain on paper towels briefly.
Serve at once with fries and sauce.
Finely grate the potatoes and squeeze out the liquid in a towel.
Mix with the egg, [[0.5 cup]] flour, garlic, [[1 tsp]] marjoram, [[1.5 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in portions of batter and flatten to thin rounds.
Cook 4 minutes per side until crisp and golden, adding oil as needed.
Drain on a plate lined with paper towels.
Serve hot, as a side or with sour cream.
Melt [[3 tbsp]] lard in a heavy pot and cook the onions 8 minutes.
Add the pork, garlic, caraway and [[1 tsp]] salt, and brown the meat for 8 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in [[1.5 tbsp]] paprika.
Add the sauerkraut, bay leaf and [[2 cup]] water. Cover and simmer on low for 75 minutes until the pork is tender.
Mix [[2 tbsp]] flour into [[0.75 cup]] sour cream until smooth, adding a ladle of hot liquid.
Stir into the goulash and simmer for 10 minutes without boiling hard.
Check the pork reaches at least 145°F (63°C). Serve with bread dumplings or potatoes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 25 minutes until tender, then peel and mash very smooth.
Cool until warm. Mix with [[1.5 cup]] flour and [[1 tsp]] salt into a soft dough.
Divide the dough into 8 equal balls.
Roll each ball very thin into a round, using flour as needed.
Heat a dry skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook each round for 1 minute per side until spotted brown. Keep them under a towel.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] ground poppy seeds with [[0.33 cup]] sugar and [[2 tbsp]] milk.
Brush each lokša with [[4 tbsp]] melted butter in total, spread with poppy mix, and roll up.
Boil the potatoes in their skins for 25 minutes. Peel while warm and mash smooth.
Cool slightly. Add the egg, [[1.5 cup]] flour and [[1 tsp]] salt and knead into a soft dough.
Roll the dough into ropes about 0.5 inch thick.
Cut the ropes into 1-inch pieces. Roll each between your palms into small spindles.
Boil in salted water for 5 minutes until they float.
Drain well and toss with [[4 tbsp]] melted butter.
Mix [[0.5 cup]] ground poppy seeds with [[0.33 cup]] sugar and sprinkle over the noodles. Serve warm.
